newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AGL sees higher year profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AGL sees higher year profit.

text.p: The Australian Gas Light Company (AGL) said on Thursday it expected profit for the year to June 30 to be higher than the previous year.
"On present indications the board expects the profit for the full year to be higher than the previous year," chairman John Phillips said in a statement accompanying half year results.

Phillips said the result for the six months to December 31, which saw net profit rise 19.6 percent to A$75.6 million, continued the solid growth trends of the past five years and confirmed AGL's ability to adapt to the continually changing market conditions in the Australian energy market.
AGL managing director Len Bleasel said AGL's two main operating businesses, energy utilities and energy trading and transmission, had both performed well during the half year.
Gas sales volumes to residential customers rose by 10.4 percent and despite a depressed new homes market 14,711 new customers were connected.
AGL said its energy utilities division, which includes AGL Gas Networks, AGL Retail Energy, AGL New Zealand and Industrial Pipe Systems, contributed A$84.3 million to earnings.

Energy Trading and Transmission made a contribution of A$28.1 million to the half year result, with the main increase coming from the newly formed AGL Wholesale Energy, which was now responsible for gas sales to AGL's major industrial customers.
Bleasel said AGL expected to finalise terms and conditions on its access to the newly deregulated natural gas market in New South Wales, Australia's most populous state.
Third part access to AGL's New South Wales gas distribution network is part of a national programme to deregulate the gas and electricity market in Australia.
Bleasel said in the electricity sector, Solaris Power, was performing to the company's expectations deliver a contribution to AGL of A$8.2 million in fees and dividends.
